taper_is_harmful_at_ss.note: three independent comparisons; both dead either way but the taper is consistently over an order of magnitude worse
taper_is_harmful_at_ss.mechanism: TESTED: stage count, not stage size. At mos_ss/27C with the m=4 converter, 2 stages big-stage2 0.001873 V, 2 stages small-stage2 0.003526 V, 4 stages 0.000035 V, 6 stages 0.000001 V. Shrinking stage 2 improves it; adding stages costs ~50x per two stages. A taper assumes full-swing inputs so each stage restores the edge; with a degraded input each stage attenuates instead and a chain multiplies the loss.
taper_is_harmful_at_ss.RETRACTED_2026_08_06_evening: Withdrawn. Every value compared is under 4 mV, at or below the stuck-pin level; ranking degrees of a dead output is not evidence. The upstream converter delivered only ~92 ps at that corner, below the minimum input width of BOTH buffers, so the comparison could not discriminate. The stage-count-not-stage-size mechanism is withdrawn with it.

superseded_criterion_2026_08_06_evening: Every figure in this package is time above 600 mV. That criterion is scored higher by a circuit that merges several bits into one wide pulse than by one that resolves them correctly, so it rewards the defect. Replaced by bit-error decoding at the bit clock against the transmitted sequence, with the comparator output decoded alongside as a reference. Under that criterion the output path reaches zero errors only at 800 ps/bit and only at the three 125 C corners; slow silicon at 27 C needs 3200 ps/bit; res_wcs at -40 C does not move at any rate tested. The amplitude and width figures here remain correct as measurements and are not evidence of function.
